page: Microsoft Azure M8ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an arm64 processor architecture and provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a high memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU, tailored for services requiring large active memory pools relative to compute threads.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, nor does it contain hardware graphics acceleration. Storage operations rely entirely on remote network storage, with architectural support for Premium Storage volumes. In qualitative terms, utilizing energy-efficient ARM-based silicon alongside a wide memory bus provides efficient resource density for workloads bottlenecked on memory capacity rather than core counts.

A key architectural consideration is the lack of local scratch space and specialized instruction sets such as AVX or AMX, requiring workloads to be compiled for arm64 execution. Microsoft Azure M8ps_v4 is suited for in-memory caching layers, memory-intensive database engines, data pipeline buffers, and enterprise backend applications compatible with ARM-based operating environments.
description: Microsoft Azure M8ps_v4 is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high-density 16.0 GB allocation per core. The server includes no GPUs and lacks onboard local storage, depending instead on external Premium Storage capabilities for persistence. By pairing ARM processor architecture with substantial memory capacity, this instance offers efficient scaling for workloads where RAM utilization dominates over compute overhead. Because it does not provision local ephemeral disks, it relies on network-attached storage architectures. Microsoft Azure M8ps_v4 is designed to run in-memory databases, key-value stores, distributed caches, and memory-heavy enterprise backend services configured for 64-bit ARM environments.
